title: Integrated Finance Playbook: Budgeting, Forecasting, Contracts, Procurement, and Revenue Recognition (2028)
author: Maya Thompson
body:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's core finance and legal procedures for annual budgeting and rolling forecasting, contract lifecycle and legal intake processes, procurement workflows, and revenue recognition / billing policy highlights. The goal is to provide a single operational reference for finance, legal, procurement, and engineering/product partners so decisions are consistent, auditable, and aligned to our revenue and cash objectives.

Key principles:
- Clear ownership and separation of duties between requesters, approvers, procurement, and legal.
- Predictability in forecasting and budgeting to support capacity (Dedicated/Private) and capital planning for GPU fleet investments.
- Contract fidelity: standard templates used whenever possible; deviations routed through Legal with documented risk assessment.
- Compliance with ASC 606 revenue recognition principles and internal billing cadence: invoices, credits, and usage reconciliation procedures maintained.

Scope and audience:
- This document applies to: finance, legal, procurement, product, engineering leads, and sales operations.
- It covers: annual budgeting process, quarterly rolling forecasting, PO and vendor procurement flows, contract intake and lifecycle, and a summary of revenue recognition and billing practices for hosted and Dedicated offerings.

Sections:
1) Budgeting and Forecasting
2) Contracts and Legal Process
3) Procurement Procedures
4) Revenue Recognition & Billing
5) Ownership, SLAs, and Audit Requirements

---

1) Budgeting and Forecasting

Purpose:
Provide a repeatable process for producing an annual budget that aligns to company strategy and a rolling quarterly forecast to support operational decision-making (capacity purchases, hiring, R&D prioritization).

Calendar and cadence:
- Annual budget kickoff: first Monday of July.
- Draft budgets from teams due: August 31.
- Finance consolidation and review cycles: September.
- Executive review & approval: October 15.
- Budget ratified: October 31.
- Rolling forecast cadence: updated monthly; quarterly formal re-forecast in the first two weeks of each quarter.

Inputs required from teams:
- Headcount plan (FTEs), compensation bands, and start dates.
- Infrastructure forecasts (GPU hrs, cloud egress), model licensing costs, and dedicated capacity commitments.
- Sales bookings and pipeline build (Sales Ops).
- One-off capital purchases and multi-year contracts.

Budget templates and assumptions:
- Finance publishes the budget workbook (XLSX) with the following tabs: Revenue, COGS, OpEx by function, CapEx, Headcount, and Hiring Plan.
- Core assumptions documented in the "Assumptions" tab (e.g., USD exchange, growth rates, average token pricing).

Approval thresholds (examples):
- Manager-level (up to $25k annually): budget owner sign-off.
- Director-level (25k-250k): FP&A & Finance manager approval.
- VP-level (250k-1M): VP + Finance director approval.
- >$1M or multi-year commitments: CFO + Legal review required.

Scenario planning and sensitivity:
- Finance will produce three scenarios for the annual budget: Base, Upside (+15% revenue), and Downside (-10% revenue).
- Teams are required to highlight line items that are discretionary vs. committed.

2) Contracts and Legal Process

Intake and triage:
1. Contract request submitted via the Contract Intake form (internal link) by the owner (sales, partnerships, or procurement). Include: counterparty name, scope, revenue impact, term length, termination rights, and requested deviations from standard master agreement.
2. Legal performs a risk triage within 3 business days and assigns a priority: Low/Standard (use template), Elevated (negotiation required), High (requires Legal Director/CFO escalation).

Standard templates and playbooks:
- SOW / Master Services Agreement (MSA) for Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Subscription License Agreement for Redwood software components in Private/on-prem bundles.
- NDA and Data Processing Agreement (DPA) templates (GDPR-compliant).

Key contract SLAs:
- Standard template review: 2 business days.
- Non-standard/negotiated contract: 7-14 business days depending on complexity.
- High-risk contracts: timeline defined at intake; Legal will notify Contract Owner.

Contract approval matrix:
- Up to $250k ARR / 12 months: Legal Counsel approval.
- $250k-3 1M ARR: Legal Counsel + Finance Manager.
- >$1M ARR or unusual risk: Legal Director + CFO required.

Redlines and negotiation guidance (for Sales):
- Prioritize limited liability caps tied to fees paid, clear data residency obligations, and termination for convenience at 60 days for pilot engagements.
- No customer-supplied indemnities without Legal approval.

Contract storage and tracking:
- All fully executed agreements must be uploaded to the contract repository (DocuSign/SharePoint reference) and tagged with: counterparty, product (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), ARR, start/end dates, renewal terms, and owner.

3) Procurement Procedures

Purchase request workflow:
1. Requestor submits a Purchase Requisition (PR) in the procurement portal including business justification, GL code, estimated cost, and preferred vendor.
2. Manager approves PR in the portal.
3. Procurement team validates vendor (vendor onboarding checklist) and issues PO or negotiates SOW.

Vendor onboarding checklist (required for all new vendors):
- W-9 or equivalent tax form.
- Insurance certificates (if providing services on-prem).
- Security questionnaire (if vendor will access customer or internal data).
- Bank details for payment and SOC2 or equivalent if handling sensitive data.

Procurement thresholds and PO requirements:
| Estimated Spend Range | Required Action | Approval Required |
|----------------------:|-----------------|------------------|
| <$10k | Requestor + Manager | No PO required; use company card or expense system |
| $10k-50k | Procurement issues PO | Manager approval + Procurement |
| $50k-250k | Procurement negotiates contract/PO | Director approval + Procurement |
| >$250k | Procurement + Legal + Finance negotiation | VP/CFO approval |

Preferred vendor negotiation tips:
- For Dedicated capacity and multi-year cloud commitments, negotiate service-level credits, exit/termination conditions, and pricing floors.
- Consolidate requests for GPU capacity procurement when possible to obtain volume discounts.

Receiving, invoicing, and payment:
- On receipt of goods/services, requestor must mark PR as "Received" in the portal within 5 business days.
- Invoices matched to PO are routed to AP for payment on standard net-30 unless otherwise negotiated.
- Exceptions (advance payments or prepayments) require Director-level approval and justification.

4) Revenue Recognition & Billing

High-level policy summary (ASC 606 aligned):
- Revenue is recognized when performance obligations are satisfied: typically at the point in time or over time depending on the product.
- Hosted API usage: recognized over time as tokens are delivered (usage-based). Deferred revenue arises from prepayments/committed capacity.
- Dedicated: recognized over time as service is delivered (monthly recognition unless contract specifies milestone-based billing).
- Private (license + maintenance): license fees recognized per contract terms; maintenance/support recognized ratably over the support term.

Billing cadence and collections:
- Standard: monthly invoicing in arrears for hosted usage and monthly recurring fees.
- Committed Dedicated capacity: invoiced monthly or upfront per contract.
- Annual enterprise agreements: invoiced per contract (annual or milestone).
- Collections escalation: 30 day past due -> automated reminder; 60 day -> Sales Ops + Finance engage; 90 day -> Legal + collections strategy.

Handling credits, refunds, and disputes:
- Dispute intake via billing@redwood.com. Finance will acknowledge within 3 business days and open a ticket.
- Temporary credits may be issued for verified outage-related SLA breaches per the SLA playbook. Permanent refunds require Finance Manager approval.

Usage reconciliation (example monthly workflow):
1. Infra telemetry and metering pipeline emits token counts and usage by customer.
2. Finance runs reconciliation: usage pipeline vs. billing system. Discrepancies >1% escalated to Billing Ops.
3. Adjustments recorded in the month following discovery and reflected on the next invoice.

Key metrics and reporting:
- Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) target: <= 45 days.
- Deferred revenue aging: report monthly with buckets 0-30 / 31-90 / >90 days.
- Billing accuracy target: 99.5% per invoice.

5) Ownership, SLAs, and Audit Requirements

RACI summary:
- Finance: owner of budgeting, forecasting consolidation, billing ops, and revenue recognition policy.
- Legal: owner of contract templates, intake triage, and risk assessment.
- Procurement: owner of vendor onboarding, POs, and supplier negotiations.
- Product/Engineering: provide forecasts for capacity and model-related licensing costs; validate delivery of services for SOW acceptance.
- Sales: owner of contract commercial terms and customer negotiations (in collaboration with Legal).

SLA and response times:
- Contract triage: Legal response within 3 business days.
- Procurement PR initial validation: 2 business days.
- Billing dispute acknowledgement: 3 business days.

Audit and documentation requirements:
- Paper trail: all approvals, POs, signed contracts, and invoices must be stored in the company repository for a minimum of 7 years.
- External audits: Finance to provide requested schedules (revrec, deferred revenue roll-forward, sample invoices) within 10 business days of request.
- Internal control: periodic review of approval matrix and segregation of duties to be performed annually by Finance and Internal Audit.

Appendices:
A. Example Contract Intake Form (fields): counterparty, product, ARR estimate, term, data residency, security flags, requested deviations, sales owner.
B. Budget Template Checklist: headcount, infrastructure, model licensing, marketing & G&A, one-time capital.
C. Quick reference: Approval matrix table, procurement thresholds, and billing contacts.

Contacts and escalation:
- Finance (FP&A & Billing Ops): finance-ops@redwood.com
- Legal (Contracts): legal-contracts@redwood.com
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.com
- Escalation: CFO (cfo@redwood.com) and General Counsel (gc@redwood.com)
